answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a self-defeating exit: epoch rewards are paid in a token redeemed through a slow, shared queue, like a marble rolling down a single narrow chute. When one honest agent redeems, the price barely moves, but when a farm tries to cash out a thousand fakes at once across the tundra of its accounts, its own selling pressure crashes the price it receives. Under a sable market rule the queue throttles redemptions and each sale lowers the next, so cloning multiplies identities yet shrinks total profit, while a single genuine agent exits at full value.
